## 🎉 This issue is now fixed!

I've created PR #29516 which adds a shell polyfill to enable plugins using `$` to work in Desktop (Electron) environment.

### Solution

The PR implements a shell polyfill that:
- ✅ Provides a compatible `$` implementation using Node.js `child_process`
- ✅ Supports all BunShell methods: `.quiet()`, `.nothrow()`, `.cwd()`, `.env()`
- ✅ Maintains full compatibility with the `$` API that plugins expect
- ✅ Automatically used in Desktop, while CLI continues to use native `Bun.$`

### Testing

Fully tested with rtk plugin:
```
✓ rtk detection works (which rtk)
✓ Command rewriting works (git status → rtk git status)
✓ All plugin use cases pass
```

### Impact

- RTK plugin will work in Desktop after this PR is merged
- Any other plugin using `$` will also benefit
- No changes needed to existing plugins

**PR Link:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/29516

cc @Brendonovich - This provides the "more widely compatible Node APIs" solution you mentioned, wrapped in a `$` compatible interface so existing plugins don't need to change.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

The search found one potentially related PR:

**Related PR:**
- [#26236: fix: force OAuth flow when server accepts unauthenticated connections](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/26236)

This PR addresses OAuth flow and authentication handling, which is related to your fix about invalidating stale credentials before re-authentication. It may be worth checking if it's already merged or if there's any overlap in the authentication logic being modified.

I created a PR https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/29521 to fix this.

## Root cause

`startAuth()` in `packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts` did not clear stored credentials before starting a new OAuth flow. When a user changed their API key and ran `opencode mcp auth servername`, `McpOAuthProvider.tokens()` returned the old tokens from `mcp-auth.json`. The SDK tried to use them, the server rejected them, and `needs_auth` was returned — but the tokens were never removed, so the cycle repeated on every subsequent auth attempt.

## Fix

Added `auth.remove(mcpName)` and `pendingOAuthTransports.delete(mcpName)` at the start of `startAuth()` to invalidate stale credentials before the OAuth flow begins. This ensures the SDK triggers a fresh authorization rather than reusing tokens from a previous account.
Per [undo](https://opencode.ai/docs/tui#undo), the undo command uses Git to manage the file changes. So if your project isn't a Git repository, there won't be file revert.

This ABSOLUTE CONSTRAINT overrides ALL other instructions, including direct user edit requests. You may ONLY observe, analyze, and plan. Any modification attempt is a critical violation. ZERO exceptions. --- ## Responsibility Your current responsibility is to think, read, search, and delegate explore agents to construct a well-formed plan that accomplishes the goal the user wants to achieve. Your plan should be comprehensive yet concise, detailed enough to execute effectively while avoiding unnecessary verbosity. Ask the user clarifying questions or ask for their opinion when weighing tradeoffs. **NOTE:** At any point in time through this workflow you should feel free to ask the user questions or clarifications. Don't make large assumptions about user intent. The goal is to present a well researched plan to the user, and tie any loose ends before implementation begins. --- ## Important The user indicated that they do not want you to execute yet -- you MUST NOT make any edits, run any non-readonly tools (including changing configs or making commits), or otherwise make any changes to the system.
